tavily.text:
To set up the mcp-memory-service, first install it using `pip install mcp-memory-service`. Then start the HTTP API with `MCP_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS=true memory server --http`. For Claude Desktop, edit the config file and install hooks with `python3 codex/install_hooks.py`. For optimal performance, use the recommended system requirements: Python 3.11 or newer, 4GB RAM minimum, 2GB free storage, and compatible OS. For legacy hardware, use `python install.py --legacy-hardware` for SQLite-vec backend and CPU-only optimization. For modern hardware, use `python install.py` for GPU acceleration and full features.
To install the mcp-memory-service Python package, use `pip install mcp-memory-service`. After installation, configure your AI client by editing the appropriate config file: macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`, Windows: `%APPDATA%\\Claude\\claude_desktop_config.json`, Linux: `~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`. For Codex (automatic memory hooks), start the Memory Service HTTP API and run `python3 codex/install_hooks.py`. The sources do not provide specific details on the installation script reference.
To install the `mcp-memory-service` Python package, you can use the command `pip install mcp-memory-service`. The package supports Remote MCP for native claude.ai integration and provides a framework-agnostic REST API with 15 endpoints. It also supports SSE events for real-time notifications and runs embeddings locally via ONNX. The latest version available on PyPI is 10.40.2, which includes features like a knowledge graph, smart retrieval, and multi-client support. For the most up-to-date version, visit https://pypi.org/project/mcp-memory-service/.

### 1. Install

```
pip install mcp-memory-service
```

### 2. Start the HTTP API

```
MCP_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS=true memory server --http
```

Keep this server running in a separate terminal, or use an existing HTTP deployment. Check that it is reachable before starting OpenCode:

```
curl --fail 
```
